title: See a QR code parked somewhere? FTC advises caution

body_markdown:
Ever pull into a parking spot, only to find that paying requires scanning a QR code? While QR codes and be a convenient way to pay for various products and services like parking,[The FTC warns](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2026/09/see-qr-code-parked-somewhere-dont-scan-ityet) that scammers have found ways to exploit them, too.


In some cases, scammers place fake QR code stickers over legitimate parking meter codes. If you scan one of these fraudulent codes, you could be directed to a fake website designed to steal your money, personal information, or both.


So, how can you protect yourself from these scams? The FTC recommends following these steps:


- **Inspect the URL link** . Many QR readers preview the link they will send you to. Make sure there are no spelling mistakes or switched letters in the link before you click.
- **Protect your phone.** Update your phone’s operating system (OS) and apps to help prevent scammy links from turning into a hack:


- [Apple Support: Update your iPhone or iPad](https://consumer.ftc.gov/now-leaving?external_url=https%3A%2F%2Fsupport.apple.com%2Fen-us%2F118575&back_url=https%3A%2F%2Fconsumer.ftc.gov%2Fconsumer-alerts%2F2026%2F09%2Fsee-qr-code-parked-somewhere-dont-scan-ityet)
- [Android Help: Check & update your Android version](https://consumer.ftc.gov/now-leaving?external_url=https%3A%2F%2Fsupport.google.com%2Fandroid%2Fanswer%2F7680439%3Fhl%3Den&back_url=https%3A%2F%2Fconsumer.ftc.gov%2Fconsumer-alerts%2F2026%2F09%2Fsee-qr-code-parked-somewhere-dont-scan-ityet)


- **Use strong passwords for your accounts.** Protect your online accounts[with strong passwords](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/creating-strong-passwords-and-other-ways-protect-your-accounts) and[multi-factor authentication](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/use-two-factor-authentication-protect-your-accounts) .


Think you scanned a bad QR code? Follow these steps:


- **Don’t interact with the scammer:** If you reach out to someone through the website you think is fake, they may try to get money or sensitive information out of you.
- **Change your password:** If you entered credentials like your username or password, immediately change them wherever you use the same password for other accounts.
- **Review your transactions:** Check your credit card and bank statements to spot transactions you didn’t make.


Then, report it to the FTC at[ReportFraud.ftc.gov](https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/) .
